svg.text: Expectancy: The One Number That Says a System Makes Money
Win rate and reward, combined into the average profit per trade -- in dollars or in R.
Expectancy = (win rate x average win) - (loss rate x average loss)
In R (always risk 1R, honour stops): (win% x average R won) - (loss% x 1R)
A real edge (positive)
45% win, avg win $300, avg loss $150:
40% win at +2R average (loss 1R):
Over 100 trades = +20R. At $100 / R,
+$2,000 -- while wrong 60% of the time.
A high win rate that still loses
60% win, avg win $80, avg loss $150:
Right most of the time, losing money
every trade -- because the losses are
far larger than the wins.
Win rate alone never decides.
The catch: expectancy is a long-run average
A positive-expectancy system can still lose 5, 10, even 20 trades in a row -- that is normal variance,
not a broken system. A losing system can also win for a while by luck. A handful of trades tells you nothing.
So: judge a system over many trades (a journal), and keep risk per trade small (1-2%, Ch3 L1)
so a normal losing streak cannot end you before the edge has time to show.
Position sizing keeps you alive through variance; discipline lets the positive expectancy actually be realised.
The plan turns an edge on paper into money in an account -- by making you trade the same positive-expectancy process every time.
